root_idea.summary: The root centers on tactile contact and the seeking or pursuit of something.
root_idea.development: The root's original orientation is seeking by hand in order to know a thing's touch; this usage developed into the broader sense of seeking or pursuing anything.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed separately as the attested Form VIII verb.

senses.definition: To touch or feel something through the outer surface of the body; to make tactile contact.
senses.usage_conditions: The sense includes direct physical contact and feeling something with the hand. In the Quranic passages concerning touching or contacting women, the expression is also subject to the interpretive range described in the following sense.

senses.definition: To have sexual intercourse, expressed euphemistically as touching a woman.
senses.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction لَامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ / لَمَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ. The same Quranic wording is also interpreted as referring to physical touching rather than intercourse.

senses.definition: To seek, search for, or pursue something.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an extended use from feeling or searching for something by hand and may refer to seeking or striving after an object, knowledge, or a destination.

senses.definition: To seek, search for, or pursue something.
senses.usage_conditions: The Form VIII verb expresses active seeking or searching; the Quranic occurrence is an imperative addressed to a group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Apprehending or coming to know a thing even without direct physical contact.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension in which لمس denotes knowledge or recognition rather than contact between substances.
A figurative or euphemistic use mentioned alongside the sense of sexual intercourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take away or destroy sight, including by attacking or putting out the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction used of sight or the eye; the reported explanations include rapidly destroying sight and aiming at the eye with a bite.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sale concluded merely by touching the garment or commodity, without seeing, inspecting, or retaining the option to return it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional and prohibited mode of bargaining in which touching makes the sale binding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To permit someone to feel or touch another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction أَلْمِسْنِي الْجَارِيَةَ, “permit me to feel or touch the girl.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To procure or arrange a woman in marriage for the speaker.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative request expressed as أَلْمِسْنِي امْرَأَةً, “marry or procure a woman for me.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel whose fatness or hump is uncertain and is examined by touch.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term refers to uncertainty about whether the camel has fat, prompting tactile examination.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person of suspected origin or lineage, or whose claim to honor has a blemish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative characterization derived from the specialized camel term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman soft to the touch.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive feminine use referring to softness of tactile feel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A want or need, especially a moderate or middling one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related forms لَمَاسَةٌ and لُمَاسَةٌ are reported for this meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road or way sought by someone who has lost the route in order to find the track of travelers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the road's being sought as a means of recovering the route.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the idiom لَا تَرُدُّ يَدَ لَامِسٍ or لَا يَرُدُّ يَدَ لَامِسٍ: a sexually available or promiscuous woman, or a man lacking resistance and regard for what is sacred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The interpretation varies with the subject: of a woman it describes not repelling a man seeking sexual access; of a man it describes lack of resistance or care for inviolable things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an alternative interpretation of the same idiom, a wife who gives out her husband's property when it is requested from her.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an alternate explanation of the expression when applied to a wife.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or surface that is felt or touched.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may also function as a verbal noun related to لمس.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Smoothed or evened by repeated passage of the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of the curved wooden parts of an ass's saddle after their unevenness has been removed by hand.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers tactile contact, tactile seeking, and apprehension without direct contact.

cautions: In 4:43 and 5:6, the construction لَامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ / لَمَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ has an attested interpretive range between physical touching and euphemistic reference to sexual intercourse.
